record.notes: CONFIRMED, unchanged. EUR 50.90 a year / 12 = EUR 4.24 a month = USD 4.75 at the ECB rate. The renewal claim holds and is stated three ways on one page: the promo banner, the invoice block and FAQ 04. Worst case exposure is 1.0x because the discount is stated as locked at renewal: there is no month 13 where the price moves. This remains the only row in the band whose sub-USD-5 monthly is a recurring rate rather than a first-term promo. Shape is 3 vCPU / 6 GiB / 55 GB / 6 TB: less RAM than the 8 GiB rows, more CPU than most of them.

extras.price_arithmetic: EUR 50.90 a year / 12 = EUR 4.2417 a month; x 1.1193 (ECB reference, 2026-10-23) = USD 4.747, rounded USD 4.75. Monthly billing is EUR 4.99 = USD 5.59, over the line. It is a VPS, so the monthly bill is the bill and there is no 730-hour multiplication.

egress.terms: Metered, not free. Plan transfer allowances: 1 TB plan = 3 TB/mo, 2 TB plan = 6 TB, 4 TB = 10 TB, 8 TB = 20 TB, 16 TB = 40 TB, all on ports 'up to 10 Gbit'. Overage is charged, not throttled: the provider, §Traffic Usage, read 'All account plans come with a predetermined monthly amount of traffic allowance. We charge 3.0EUR additional per TB over the allowance, unless otherwise agreed upon.' (https://alphavps.com/terms). The backup-storage landing page separately advertises 'No egress fees, no vendor lock-in' and 'EGRESS €0 - FLAT'. Treat egress as €3/TB metered.

record.interface_detail: sftp, rsync, nfs, rest (self-hosted: MinIO/SeaweedFS/Nextcloud on the VPS, or WebDAV)
record.tooling: Rclone over SFTP/WebDAV, BorgBackup, Restic, rsync. No native S3. You host your own gateway.
record.chaining: Best of the VPS class for the archive half: root KVM, so AList/OpenList or MinIO can be installed and fronted by Cloudflare for cache-covered egress. Not usable as a raw S3 origin without running MinIO.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: none (block device). RAID-60 with NVMe read cache. 14-day money-back on FIRST order only, excludes promos, crypto, and orders from China.
record.reliability_note: Bulgarian operator (DA International Group Ltd.), own AS203380 since 2013, 99.9% uptime SLA in the published SLA. Long-running positive sentiment on LowEndTalk; one 2022 thread documents a bad provisioning experience but not data loss.
